Subject: Post-demo model shortlist & ops tradeoffs — Coriolis POC

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the model shortlist + ops considerations we discussed on the call. Attaching the CSV with the benchmark traces and a prompt set we used for the demo.

Summary (short):
- Goals: high turn-around for clinician queries (SLO: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms), throughput ~120 QPS peak, strict PHI handling (no persistent logs)
- Primary ask: recommended model(s) for initial POC that balance latency, cost, and clinical QA defensibility

Recommended shortlist (tradeoffs):
1) LlamaX-13B (quantized int8) — Best latency/cost balance on A100-like infra. p50 ~ 65ms, p95 ~ 210ms at 128-token responses; lowest infra cost with modest accuracy drop on structured clinical extractions. Good fit if you want fast iteration and lower committed spend.
2) MedLM-7B-adapt (FP16) — Stronger clinical accuracy on domain prompts, higher per-token cost and latency (p50 ~ 95ms, p95 ~ 310ms); recommended for validation steps where recall on entities matters.
3) GPT-Refine-3B (distilled + RL finetune) — Lowest latency and easiest to run at edge; quality can be variable on rare entity patterns but excellent for routing/triage tasks.

Operational notes / risks:
- Caching: with prefix caching for common templates we can reduce effective cost by ~25% (see benchmark_results.csv).
- Regression guardrails: we recommend a small eval harness (10k clinical prompts) run on every model change — we included a baseline prompt set in prompt_set_v1.txt.
- PHI & retention: for POC we propose token-only RAM handling + no disk persistence; this requires a short-term private deployment or Dedicated pool for auditability.

Questions for you (helps us size and propose):
1) Confirm average/peak QPS expected during hours of operation (you mentioned 100–150).
2) Can we run a small sample of de-identified clinical prompts for our eval (expected size ~5k prompts)?
3) Any procurement constraints on using dedicated hardware vs hosted API for the POC?

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm QPS and approval to run 5k eval prompts (this week)
- Us: share a cost/latency estimate for both Hosted vs Dedicated (attached PDF) and an A/B plan for LlamaX-13B (quant) vs MedLM-7B-adapt
- Schedule: recommend a 45-min follow-up early next week to lock the POC configuration and timeline

Attachments: benchmark_results.csv (traces + latency buckets), prompt_set_v1.txt (baseline prompts), cost_estimates_summary.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

—
Naomi Feldman

Naomi — really useful summary, thanks. Quick answers to your questions:
1) Peak QPS: target ~120 QPS during clinic surge windows; baseline 20–30 QPS otherwise.
2) We can provide the 5k de-identified prompts but need our privacy team to sign off on the sample delivery mechanism (should be S3 with restricted access).
3) Procurement: initial preference is hosted evaluation (faster), but security team will require either dedicated tenant or private deployment for anything with PHI. They asked for SOC2 Type II evidence and a brief data flow diagram.

Can you send the SOC2 link and the short infra comparison (hosted vs dedicated) by EOD? I scheduled a follow-up for Mon 10AM ET if that still works.

Also, the clinical QA lead Tom will join the call and wants to review the prompt set before the meeting.

—
Sarah Liu

Looping in a couple of ops points based on the benchmark CSV Naomi attached.

On Wed, Mar 22, 2028 at 5:05 PM Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Summary (short):
> - Goals: high turn-around for clinician queries (SLO: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms), throughput ~120 QPS peak, strict PHI handling (no persistent logs)

Internal ops recommendation:
- For the POC I’d propose deploying LlamaX-13B (int8 quant) on a small Dedicated pool (2-3 GPUs depending on load profile). That gives reproducible latency and lets us guarantee no persistent tokens in customer-managed environment. We can run MedLM-7B-adapt in Hosted for the QA comparisons to avoid up-front infra commits.
- Cost delta: Dedicated pool (reserved) for LlamaX quant is ~40% cheaper than hosted bursts at peak for the same latency profile; I'll include a simple cost delta in the doc Naomi is prepping.
- Regression guardrails: Karthik, suggest we prepare a lightweight eval job in CI that runs nightly on the baseline prompt set and posts diffs to the dashboard link. Monica, can you prep the initial monitoring thresholds for entity-level recall drop (e.g., >5% drop triggers an alert)?

Ben
Sr Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
